newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma blocks access to Suu Kyi's home again.
newsitem.headline: Burma blocks access to Suu Kyi's home again.

text.p: Burmese military authorities barred access to the road leading to opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi's home early on Saturday to prevent her from holding gatherings or meeting people, witnesses said.
Traffic wardens blocked off the access roads to University Avenue where Suu Kyi's home is located.

A spokesman for Suu Kyi told Reuters that the barring of access had prevented a visiting representative of the Geneva-based World Council of Churches (WCC) from coming to meet her on Saturday. The visitor was not identified.
Suu Kyi was busy holding meetings with other senior leaders of her National League for Democracy (NLD), he said.

Last weekend, Suu Kyi's motorcade was attacked by a large group of stone-throwing young men believed to have been engineered by the Union Solidarity and Development Association which is an officially-recognised body.
The ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) said it was investigating the incident but Suu Kyi said the SLORC had orchestrated the attack.
The United States and the European Union in separate statements on Friday warned the Burmese government against allowing further violence against Suu Kyi this weekend.
A government spokesman said he did not know of any WCC official visiting Burma and had heard rumours that Suu Kyi had been invited to attend a function at a Rangoon church.
But the Myanmar Council of Churches had officially stated that it had not invited her to any function, he added.
"Some roads leading to her house are closed but it all quiet here with everybody busy making preparations for the launch of visit Myanmar Year on Monday," he said.
Burma launches the tourism promotion on Monday. Elaborate preparations, including hotel and airport constructions, have been made to promote the event.
